analysis.note: Ablative of cause/source: “out of fear”; Śaṅkara supplies the feared persons as Karṇa and others.
Ablative singular, construed with uparatam: “from battle.”
Accusative masculine singular predicate to tvām; kta-participle from upa-√ram, “withdrawn/ceased.”
Simple future, 3rd plural Ātmanepada in form, active in sense: “they will think.”
Second-person pronoun, object of maṃsyante; masculine supplied from its male referent Arjuna and agreement with uparatam, though the form itself is not gender-distinct.
Subject of maṃsyante; used substantively of great chariot-warriors.

analysis.note: Relative genitive plural referring to Duryodhana and the other mahārathas: “in whose eyes / by whom.”
Second-person pronoun, subject of bhūtvā and yāsyasi; masculine supplied from its male referent Arjuna and agreement with bahumataḥ, though the form itself is not gender-distinct.

samasa.vigraha: bahu, bahubhir guṇair yuktaḥ iti, mataḥ

analysis.note: Nominative masculine singular agreeing with tvam; final visarga becomes -o before bh-. Śaṅkara explains it as “regarded as endowed with many qualities.”

verification.detail: compound stem bahumata as Pum/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Simple future, second singular: “you will go/come.”
Accusative goal/state with yāsyasi: “lowliness, insignificance,” glossed by Śaṅkara as laghu-bhāva.

justifications.decision: The ablative bhayāt is causal, and Śaṅkara explicitly supplies karṇādibhyaḥ as the object/source of fear and excludes kṛpā as the motive. Therefore the translation should not leave the withdrawal as noble compassion.
options_considered: fear of Karṇa and the others
justifications.chosen: “Out of fear of Karṇa and the others,” not “from compassion.”

evidence.quote: bhayāt karṇādibhyaḥ raṇāt yuddhāt uparataṃ nivṛttaṃ maṃsyante cintayiṣyanti na kṛpayeti
evidence.translation: “Out of fear—of Karṇa and the others; from raṇa, that is, battle; uparata, withdrawn; they will think, i.e. they will consider—not through pity.”

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara glosses raṇāt as yuddhāt, uparatam as nivṛttam, and maṃsyante as cintayiṣyanti. Thus tvām is the object of “they will think,” with uparatam as its predicate complement.
justifications.chosen: “Withdrawn from battle” as the predicate thought by the mahārathas.

evidence.quote: raṇāt yuddhāt uparataṃ nivṛttaṃ maṃsyante cintayiṣyanti
evidence.translation: “From raṇa, from battle; uparata, withdrawn; maṃsyante, they will think.”

justifications.decision: The commentary identifies the subject mahārathāḥ not as literal “great chariots” but as persons, specifically Duryodhana and others.
options_considered: Duryodhana and his party as the mahārathas
justifications.chosen: mahārathāḥ are the Kaurava-side great warriors, Duryodhana and the rest.

justifications.decision: Rather than taking bahumataḥ as merely “thought by many” or socially popular, Śaṅkara explains the content of the esteem: Arjuna is regarded as endowed with many qualities.
options_considered: well liked in a vague sense
esteemed as endowed with many qualities
justifications.chosen: bahumataḥ means highly esteemed as possessing many virtues/qualities.

evidence.quote: yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ duryodhanādīnāṃ bahu-mato bahubhir guṇair yuktaḥ ity evaṃ mataḥ bahumato bhūtvā
evidence.translation: “And for whom—you, among Duryodhana and the others—bahu-mata: thought thus, ‘endowed with many qualities’; having become bahumata.”

justifications.decision: The object of yāsyasi is not speed, dexterity, or physical lightness; Śaṅkara glosses lāghava as laghu-bhāva, a fall into being ‘light’ or slight in esteem.
justifications.chosen: lāghavam is lowliness/insignificance, the state of being slight.

evidence.translation: “Then you will go to lāghava, the state of being slight.”

translation:
Out of fear of Karṇa and the others, not from compassion,
the great chariot-warriors—Duryodhana and the rest—
will think you withdrawn from battle;
and, having been highly esteemed in their eyes—
regarded as possessed of many virtues—
you will come to lowliness (lāghava), the state of being slight.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might take bhayāt as vague fear and miss Śaṅkara’s explicit “fear of Karṇa and the others,” as well as the contrast “not through compassion.”
It might render mahārathāḥ generically, or even as literal chariots, rather than as Duryodhana and the other great warriors.
It might translate bahumataḥ as “thought by many” or simply “popular,” whereas Śaṅkara explains it as being regarded as endowed with many qualities.
It might choose a dictionary sense of lāghava such as speed, lightness, or dexterity; the bhāṣya requires “lowliness/insignificance,” laghu-bhāva.
analyzer_disagreements: raṇāt: ByT5 marks raṇa as masculine; in the battle sense, Śaṅkara’s gloss raṇāt yuddhāt and the supplied MW entry support neuter raṇa here. The ablative singular form is identical either way.
uparatam: ByT5 gives lemma uparam; for the required subanta analysis I record the inflected participial stem uparata, while noting its derivation from upa-√ram.
mahārathāḥ: ByT5 outputs mahā + rathāḥ as compound part plus noun; I treat the printed form as a single inflected compound stem mahāratha.

bahumato/bahumataḥ: ByT5 outputs bahu + mataḥ separately and lemmatizes mataḥ to √man; I treat the printed sandhi-form as one inflected compound stem bahumata, with mata as the kta-participle within the compound.
tvām and tvam: ByT5 gives second-person pronoun case/number without gender; I supply masculine because the referent is Arjuna and the agreeing predicates are masculine uparatam and bahumataḥ.
mula: bhayād raṇād uparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ | yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
commentary_lines: bhayāt karṇādibhyaḥ raṇāt yuddhāt uparataṃ nivṛttaṃ maṃsyante cintayiṣyanti na kṛpayeti tvāṃ mahārathāḥ duryodhana-prabhṛtayaḥ |
yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ duryodhanādīnāṃ bahu-mato bahubhir guṇair yuktaḥ ity evaṃ mataḥ bahumato bhūtvā punar yāsyasi lāghavaṃ laghu-bhāvam ||bhgs_2.35||
